newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine PM proposes scrapping JV tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine PM proposes scrapping JV tax breaks.

text.p: Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Tuesday he had presented parliament with a draft law which would scrap tax breaks to some joint ventures.
"Yesterday I passed on a draft law to (parliament) on scrapping Article Seven, to put all businesses on an equal footing," he told parliament.

Lazarenko said the government had analysed the work of 146 major joint ventures in areas including gas, oil, coal, alcohol and tobacco. "Non-payments (to the budget) stand at about four billion hryvnias," he said.

He did not make clear exactly which businesses would be affected, but Article Seven refers to a law on profit taxes which freed joint ventures registered before the start of 1995 from taxes for five years.
Last year another law on foreign investment was passed which allowed some business projects with foreign investments to be freed from tax payments.

Lazarenko, who has broad support from conservatives reluctant to pass tax reforms underpinning the delayed 1997 budget, said the government wanted to introduce a sliding scale of subsidies "not like today where you just have to invest $50,000 and you pay no taxes".
He said parliament could start looking at scrapping tax breaks and amending other laws on such subsidies on Wednesday.
He said non-payments due to other forms of tax breaks stood at about 6.1 billion hryvnias.
